svg.title: Learned recovery from partial rotor faults in PX4 quadrotors
svg.desc: A line drawing of a quadrotor with rotor 3 highlighted. PX4's built-in failure detector stayed silent on all 178 mild-fault flights. The learned policy finishes 98 percent versus 29 percent of missions at 20 to 35 percent thrust loss, and 21 versus 1 percent just below the hover limit, across 9,054 pre-registered PX4 flights.

g.text: Learned recovery from partial rotor faults
Trained in Isaac Lab, judged with PX4 in the loop. A mission-level policy above an unmodified autopilot.
of its thrust raises no alarm.
Isaac Lab, PyTorch port of PX4's controller
Speed, altitude, when to land. Never the motors.
Isaac Lab → versioned spec files → PX4 v1.17 SITL, Gazebo, ROS 2 |GRU detector → PPO policy → unmodified PX4 autopilot
Negative results, reported. The policy does not reduce crashes, and a perfect, delayed or absent detector changes no outcome measurably.
